answer: Sybil attacks fail when each agent must lock a refundable bond, tied to a scarce external credential, before its attestations count. Picture the registry as an onyx ledger: any identity caught double-signing is slashed, so conjuring a sable swarm of fake agents costs real capital per head. Honest consensus then rests on a basalt layer of staked, auditable deposits, cheap for peers to verify yet ruinous to forge at scale.
